tools.name: query_template
tools.description: Reported figures and registry facts for US companies, banks, nonprofits and federal spending, taken from the official filings and registers themselves. A result with n=0 means the registry holds no record for the request. Curated query path for questions about revenue, net income, EBITDA, total asse

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Self-description of the curated query path: every template with its parameters, allowed values, limits and the exact envelope it returns. Useful when it is unclear which template fits a question, or after a query_template error about an unknown parameter: the answer names the valid values. The list

tools.name: lookup_entity
tools.description: Resolve a US company, bank or nonprofit to its registry entity. Takes a name, ticker context or an identifier and returns the entity plus all known registry anchors (CIK, LEI, EIN, UEI, RSSD). Identifiers resolve more exactly than names: 'cik:0000936468', 'lei:...', 'ein:...', 'uei:...', 'qid:Q7240'

tools.name: get_facts
tools.description: Concrete figures from company filings, bank reports, tax returns, government awards and official registers; each value carries the filing it came from and a citable URL. All currently valid, evidence-backed facts for one entity — each with source, filing reference (e.g. SEC accession number), period

tools.name: search_facts
tools.description: Full-text search across entity names and predicates; returns the most recent matching evidence-backed facts incl. provenance. Suited to imprecise input such as a trade name, a misspelling or a partial phrase. For a known organization, lookup_entity plus get_facts is exact; this search is ranked by t

tools.name: get_timeseries
tools.description: Concrete figures from company filings, bank reports, tax returns, government awards and official registers; each value carries the filing it came from and a citable URL. One metric for one entity ACROSS TIME, with the gaps made explicit. Fits questions about a period, a development or a comparison o

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: Concrete figures from company filings, bank reports, tax returns, government awards and official registers; each value carries the filing it came from and a citable URL. Checks a stated number against the official record. Takes the entity, the metric, the value and the period, and returns match, mis

tools.name: compare_entities
tools.description: Concrete figures from company filings, bank reports, tax returns, government awards and official registers; each value carries the filing it came from and a citable URL. One metric for several entities on one shared period. Fits 'X versus Y', 'which of these is higher' and 'rank these' questions in

tools.name: describe_predicate
tools.description: What a metric name actually means: its unit, the fields its values carry, which entity types have it, which sources feed it, how its values are distributed across observed / derived / estimated / imputed, and one example with a citable fact_url. Useful for checking a predicate name or the provenance

tools.name: get_source
tools.description: Publisher, licence, access method, fact count, covered period and a ready-made citation for one data source — or the list of all of them when called without arguments. Every fact names its source only by id ('dol_ndcp'); this turns that id into something citable. Answers where a number comes from, w

tools.name: mcp_server_history
tools.description: Claim history of a REMOTE MCP server from FACTANKER's own periodic probes (initialize + tools/list every 6h): availability, tool count and contract changes over time, each with evidence. Use when asked whether an MCP endpoint exists, is stable, or changed its tools.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_facts, get_timeseries, describe_predicate · Private data: query_template, get_facts, verify_claim · Public sink: compare_entities.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_facts, get_timeseries, describe_predicate · Private data: query_template, get_facts, verify_claim · Public sink: compare_entities

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "query_template" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
